title: Induction step for topology-comparison vanishing
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with two Grothendieck topologies $\tau$ and $\tau'$ with every $\tau'$-covering also a $\tau$-covering, a class $\mathcal P$ of morphisms, and weak Serre subcategories $\mathcal A'_X$ of abelian $	au'$-sheaves satisfying: (i) $\mathcal P$ is stable under base change; (ii) relocalization inverse images preserve the $\mathcal A'_X$; (iii) every object of $\mathcal A'_X$ is a $	au$-sheaf; (iv) every higher direct image along a morphism in $\mathcal P$ of an object of $\mathcal A'_X$ remains in the corresponding weak Serre subcategory; and (v) every $	au$-cover has a refinement by a $	au'$-cover, a singleton $	au$-cover in $\mathcal P$, and a final $	au'$-cover. Let $\epsilon_X$ be the comparison morphism of slice topoi and let $\mathcal A_X$ be the inverse-image class. For $r\ge0$, write $(V_r)$ for the assertion that $R^i\epsilon_{X,*}H=0$ for every $X$, every $H\in\mathcal A_X$, and $1\le i\le r$. Then $(V_r)$ implies $(V_{r+1})$. The category-size convention, the two slice sites and their derived cohomology, the comparison geometric morphism, and its sheafification are those of [def-weil-size-convention], [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], [def-trf-geometric-morphism], and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification].
